messages.subject: repetition/broadcast vs. assignment?
parts:
I just wrote some broadcast functions that I'd like
to add to Stan's modeling language. Any comments or
suggestions on naming -- I think the R-style name
repX() is simpler than broadcastX().

In Stan's notation, I'm proposing the following:

1. repeat elements to fill 1D, 2D, and 3D arrays:

For T = real, int, vector, row_vector and matrix:

T[] rep_array(T x, int n);

T[,] rep_array(T x, int m, int n);

T[,,] rep_array(T x, int k, int m, int n);


2. repeat elements to fill vector, row vectors, and matrices:

vector rep_vector(real x, int m);

row_vector rep_row_vector(real x, int n);

matrix rep_matrix(real x, int m, int n);

3. broadcast vectors and row vectors up to matrices

matrix rep_matrix(vector x, int n);

matrix rep_matrix(row_vector y, int m);

They're all done and tested in the matrix lib, but I haven't
added the function signatures to Stan.

Given that all of our vectors and arrays are declared with
dimensions, I could also just generalize the assignment
function:

real x;
real x1[4];
real x2[5,6];
real x3[7,8,9];
vector[3] v;
row_vector[4] rv;
matrix[3,4] m;

x1 <- x;
x2 <- x;
x3 <- x;

v <- x;
rv <- x;
m <- x;

m <- v; // Danger, Will Robinson!!!
m <- rv;

Plus all the array-of-matrix assignments, like

vector[3] v2[2,4];

v2 <- v;

# v2 <- 0; // illegal in this proposal, but could be added

Whatever we do with assignment, I think it's important that
the implicit assignment in a function call should work the same
way. Specifically, if we allow implicit broadcasts in assignment,
we should allow the same implicit broadcasts in function calls.

I believe we decided broadcasting vectors or row vectors
to matrices would be too confusing. But are the array and
primitive matrix broadcasts OK?

- Bob
